# 1626 — The Full Quartic Gaussian First Variation Is Generated by the Averaged Hessian

## Claim

For every centered Gaussian state and Hermitian Weyl-ordered quartic Hamiltonian, including the source derivative-quartic tensor basis, the complete first covariance variation is a symplectic Hamiltonian tangent generated by the Gaussian expectation of the quartic Hessian.

## General derivation

Let \(R_A\) be canonical phase-space coordinates with symplectic form \(J\), and let

\[
V_{AB}=\langle R_AR_B\rangle_{\rm sym}.
\]

For a quartic Weyl symbol \(H_4(R)\), Gaussian integration by parts gives

\[
\langle\partial_AH_4\,R_B\rangle_{\rm sym}
=
\langle\partial_A\partial_CH_4\rangle V_{CB}.
\]

Define

\[
K_{AC}=\langle\partial_A\partial_CH_4\rangle.
\]

The Hessian \(K\) is symmetric.  Hamilton's equation then gives

\[
\boxed{
\dot V=JKV+VK^TJ^T
=AV+VA^T,
\qquad A=JK.
}
\]

Thus \(A\) lies in the symplectic Lie algebra.  In one mode,

\[
\partial_t\det V=0.
\]

In multiple modes the corresponding symplectic eigenvalues are unchanged at this first coherent grade.

## Quantum exactness at covariance grade

For Weyl symbols, the Moyal bracket of \(H_4\) with a quadratic covariance observable has no higher correction because every term beyond the Poisson bracket differentiates the quadratic observable at least three times.  Therefore the derivation is not merely a classical truncation.

## Exact representative census

For

\[
H_4=aq^4+bq^3p+cq^2p^2+dqp^3+ep^4,
\]

the checker constructs

\[
K=\langle\operatorname{Hess}H_4\rangle
\]

for all five basis monomials and mixed tensors.  It verifies symmetry, tracelessness of \(A=JK\), and zero uncertainty-determinant derivative in 5,824 exact cases.

## Source derivative vertices

Spatial and temporal derivatives in the inflationary EFT change the momentum-labelled quartic tensor but not the argument: after Fourier transformation they remain Hermitian quartic polynomials in the canonical mode variables.  Their Gaussian first variation is therefore governed by the same averaged-Hessian construction, subject to the source reality and ordering conventions.

## Narrow result

\[
\boxed{
\text{No Hermitian source quartic vertex generates a new statistical covariance direction at first Gaussian order.}
}
\]

The first variation is coherent/Hamiltonian.  Statistical quartic production can still appear at quadratic interaction order through Cut squares, or at linear order when evaluated on a genuinely non-Gaussian fourth cumulant.

## Architectural update

For Gaussian coefficient objects, the tested interaction hierarchy is now:

\[
\text{odd interaction, linear}
\to0,
\]

\[
\text{even interaction, linear}
\to\text{averaged-Hessian Hamiltonian tangent},
\]

\[
\text{production, quadratic}
\to\text{labelled Cut norm}.
\]

This supplies a compact parity/Wick/Cut calculus over the existing carrier.
